items.title: Canada to support 200 Mozambican SMEs
items.summary: Maputo, 16 Oct (AIM) – The Canadian government, through its initiative “Trade for Resilient, Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth” (TRISEG), will support 200 Mozambican small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), focusing on strengthening business competitiveness, export capacity, digital transformation and climate resilience. The project, which is expected to cover 60 percent of businesses owned or led by women, is Funded by Global Affairs Canada (GAC) and implemented by TFO Canada in partnership with the Mozambique’s Institute for the Promotion of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (IPEME). TRISEG is a regional initiative to Empower SMEs in Developing Countries. In Africa, it covers eight countries: Mozambique, Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Kenya, Madagascar, Nigeria, Senegal and Zambia. Speaking at the project launch ceremony, Pascale Thivierge, Head of Cooperation at the High Commission of Canada in Mozambique, reaffirmed Canada’s commitment to strengthening economic and trade relations with Mozambique.

items.title: Mozambique: Grain Institute explores cooperation opportunities at Trade Expo Indonesia
items.summary: The Mozambique Grain Institute (ICM), represented by its Director-General, Luís Jobe Fazenda, is participating in the 41st edition of Trade Expo Indonesia (TEI), the largest trade and investment platform in Southeast Asia, taking place from 14 to 18 October at the Indonesia Convention Exhibition (ICE), in Greater Jakarta Photo: Instituto de Cereais de Moçambique, IP The ICM is part of the official delegation of the Ministry of Economy, headed by the Secretary of State for Trade, António Grispos As a central player in the agricultural marketing value chain, the ICM is taking part in this global forum to develop cooperation opportunities covering everything from strategic supply to the final marketing of products.

items.title: Populist Czech PM Babis goes empty-handed in Senate elections
items.summary: Opposition parties still control the Czech Senate, in a major blow to Prime Minister Andrej Babis' and his governing coalition The ruling coalition of populist billionaire Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis has failed to win a single seat in elections in the Senate The result means pro-Western opposition parties control the chamber, the upper house of parliament The election on Saturday was the first electoral test for Babis after he won parliamentary elections in October 2025 that returned him to power after a break of four years since his first term as premier Final results from the two-day ballot showed that candidates directly linked to the opposition parties won 22 of the 27 seats up for grabs in the 81-member Senate, retaining a previous opposition majority The centrist ANO (or YES) movement led by Babis failed to win any more seats, leaving it with 14 Senate lawmakers Babis called the result "catastrophic." items.title: Revenue from LNG is for current development and future generations – Finance Minister
items.summary: Maputo, 16 Oct (AIM) – The Mozambican Government has stressed that revenue from liquefied natural gas (LNG) production will be used both to finance the country’s current development and to create wealth for future generations. “The Mozambican Government’s objective is indeed to ensure that revenue from natural gas can generate intergenerational wealth. The Sovereign Wealth Fund Law is already producing tangible results by establishing a division of LNG revenue between public expenditure and savings”, said Carla Loveira, Finance Minister. “We do not want all the resources to be entirely consumed by the current budget”, she added. Under the model currently in force, around 60 percent of revenue is channelled to the State Budget, while the remaining 40 percent goes into a savings account managed by the Bank of Mozambique. According to the minister, the funds are already financing major infrastructure projects.

items.title: India: CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke released after detention
items.summary: Two other prominent CJP leaders are set to be released on Sunday. India has seen huge rallies calling on the country's top election official to step down over alleged manipulation of voter rolls Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), was released on Saturday, a day after he was detained by the Delhi police during protests against the election authority in India The 31-year-old youth leader was detained while he was trying to join the protest rally which the CJP movement had called in the capital's central Connaught Place district The movement published a photo of him on X in which it referred to Dipke as "a free man." "Abhijeet Dipke released," CJP legal affairs chief Ratna Singh said on social media Singh said Dipke was released after agreeing to certain conditions.

items.title: Mozambique: ANE awards 20.6 billion meticais for Inhambane and Sofala road contracts
items.summary: According to the contract award notices published by ANE’s provincial delegations, the contracts concern new lots for road engineering and paving projects, five of which are located in Inhambane province, in southern Mozambique, and four in Sofala, in the centre of the country The awards fall under the 2026–2031 Accelerated National Road Rehabilitation and Construction Programme, known as “More Roads – 2031”, and cover national and regional road links In Inhambane province, the contracts total 285 kilometres and 10,104,807,009 meticais (€143.6 million) The contracts were awarded to a consortium comprising the companies Maripoma Entreprise Limitada, from Mozambique, Maripoma Entreprise Limitada, from Ghana, CC Building Limitada and GWIC Moçambique Limitada The largest lot in Inhambane covers the 70-kilometre Sitila–Funhalouro section of road R444, awarded for 2,469,027,132 meticais (€35 million) On the same road corridor, the 40-kilometre Massinga–Sitila section was awarded for 1,612,980,998 meticais (€22.9 million) On national road N222, the 58-kilometre Mapinhane–Macumene section…
